//: First-load (cold-cache) eager-import-closure limits for the webapp, checked by packages/dev-tools/tools/check-first-load-size.mjs after a webapp build. pageEagerKb = static import graph of index.html; workerEagerKb = static import graph of the kernel-worker entry.
//delta: maxDeltaKb is the PRIMARY gate: a PR may not grow either eager graph by more than this much versus its own merge-base, which the checker builds and measures on the same machine in the same run. Relative, so it fails only PRs that actually regress and never drifts with the platform. 4 kB was calibrated against real traffic, not guessed: eight in-flight PRs measured 0.00-1.54 kB, while a deliberately staged regression (a static `unpdf` import in the boot-critical supplemental-commands index) measured +7.0 kB. 4 kB sits in that gap.
//ceiling: The ceilings are the SECONDARY gate and the human-owned line in the sand. A delta gate alone lets many small under-threshold PRs creep the graph upward forever; these bound the total. They are NOT ratchets to nudge when a build goes red — raising one is a deliberate decision about cold-boot payload and needs a reason in the PR body. Tighten them freely as the graphs shrink.
//delta-raised: Raised 4 -> 5 for the biscotti guest-seat subsystem (PR #2535, 2026-08-28). NOT a hoist: the instruction markdown, the approver agent, and the whole directed-approval flow are behind first-use imports and verifiably absent from the worker bundle; the +4.2 kB that remains is code on the paths it gates (turn-gate state, the adaptTool hook, approval-router scoping). Every lazy-loading lever was taken first, and removing the boot wiring entirely bought more than byte-shaving did. This is a ceiling-style deliberate decision, not a ratchet to nudge: the next PR that comes in over 4 kB should be treated as a regression and investigated, not waved through, and this should be put back to 4 once the subsystem has landed.
